SCHOLARSHIP OPPORTUNITIES); AND (5) TO IMPLEMENTTEACHING OPPORTUNITIES TO SU STUDENTS IN THE COLLEGE OF AG THAT PROVIDE COMMUNITY-BASEDMENTORSHIP OPPORTUNITIES SPECIALIZED AG COURSES FOCUSING ON HORTICULTURE AND ITS RELATIONTO SOCIOLOGY SERVICE-LEARNING HOURS AND STUDENT INTERNSHIPS. INSTRUCTION INVOLVES BOTHCLASSROOM AND HANDS-ON HORTICULTURAL ACTIVITIES. CERTIFICATES ARE AWARDED UPON SUCCESSFULCOMPLETION OF THE PROGRAM. THE LIFE CHANGING MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH TO THIS PROJECT WILLALLOW YOUTH PARTICIPANTS TO GAIN HORTICULTURAL AND NUTRITIONAL KNOWLEDGE MENTAL HEALTHINTERPERSONAL SOCIAL AND WORKFORCE SKILLS TO PROVIDE A PATHWAY TO HIGHER EDUCATION. SU AGSTUDENTS HAVE QUALITY MENTORSHIP INTERNSHIP AND SERVICE-LEARNING HANDS-ON OPPORTUNITIES.THUS POSITIONING BOTH SETS OF STUDENTS UP FOR A HEALTHY AND PRODUCTIVE LIFESTYLE WITHAGRICULTURE AS ITS BACKBONE.

SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CENTER UTILIZES THE SECTION 1445 FUNDING TO ADVANCE ITS AGENDA ASSOCIATED WITH FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL PROJECTS BENEFITTING THE STATE OF LOUISIANA'S STAKEHOLDERS, AS REFLECTED IN ITS APPROVED 5-YEAR PLAN OF WORK (POW). THE POW CONSISTS OF A CONSOLIDATED AND INTEGRATED PLAN FOR RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS AT BOTH SOUTHERN AND LOUISIANA STATE UNIVERSITIES. THE MISSION OF SUAREC IS TO ENHANCE THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR PEOPLE IN LOUISIANA THROUGH MISSION-ORIENTED BASIC AND APPLIED RESEARCH THAT ADDRESSES SCIENTIFIC, TECHNOLOGICAL, SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND CULTURAL NEEDS OF ITS CITIZENS. TO ADDRESS EMERGING ISSUES OF ITS STAKEHOLDERS, EMPHASIS IS PLACED IN FIVE PROGRAMMING AREAS: (1) FAMILY AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT: FOCUSING OF ISSUES AFFECTING INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT; DISASTER, EPIDEMIC AND PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS, MITIGATION AND RECOVERY; RISK AWARENESS; SUSTAINABLE HOUSING; AGRISECURITY; AND AGRI-TOURISM. (2). FOOD SECURITY <(>&<)> SYSTEM: FOCUSED ON INCREASING THE PROFITABILITY OF LOUISIANA'S ANIMAL, PLANT, AND AQUACULTURE SYSTEMS AND IMPROVED FOOD ACCESSIBILITY, AFFORDABILITY, POLICY; FOOD SAFETY, TO INCLUDE SEAFOOD, PRODUCE, AND PROCESSED COMMODITIES - SAFETY, CERTIFICATION PROGRAMS, FARM FINANCING, AND VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS USING THE NEWLY TRADEMARKED 'SUNFOODS' DESIGNATION. (3). NATURAL RESOURCES <(>&<)> ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY: FOCUSES ON CONSERVATION AND PRESERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND PARTICULARLY THE HEALTH OF STATE'S GRAZING LANDS, STATE'S WILDLIFE, WETLAND PLANTS, WATER, WASTE MANAGEMENT, LANDSCAPES, EFFECTS FORESTRY, INDUSTRY, FEEDSTOCKS, ALTERNATIVE BIOFUELS, BAGASSE ALTERNATIVES, BIOMASS PROCESSING AND THE IMPACTS ON THE ENVIRONMENT. (4) OBESITY, HEALTH <(>&<)> WELLNESS FOCUSES ON INCREASED CONSUMPTION OF 'CLEAN' FOODS WHILE REDUCING INTAKES OF 'ULTRA-PROCESSED' FOODS AND DEVELOPING PROGRAMS ADDRESSING DECREASING OBESITY LEVELS IN ALL AGES, INCREASING CONSUMPTION OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES, INCREASING TIME IN PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES; COMPLETE PHYSICAL, MENTAL, AND SOCIAL WELL-BEING OF ALL AGES; POLICY, SYSTEM AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE; AND RELATED TO NUTRITION/HEALTH/WELLNESS ISSUES TO INCLUDE EPIDEMIC AND PANDEMIC PREVENTION; AND (5) YOUTH DEVELOPMENT: FOCUSES ON PROVIDING LOUISIANA YOUTH WITH POSITIVE DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES AND ACTIVITIES TO BUILD INSPIRATIONAL LEADERS AND HEALTHY CITIZENS. THESE PROGRAMS AND ASSOCIATED OUTCOMES ARE ACCESSIBLE TO STAKEHOLDERS ACROSS THE ENTIRE STATE OF LOUISIANA AND DISSEMINATED IN SEVERAL MODALITIES, INCLUDING RESEARCH CONDUCTED ON CAMPUS AND EXPERIMENT STATIONS, AND OFF-CAMPUS AT DIFFERENT STAKEHOLDER AND PARTNER FARMS AND WORK SITES. FACULTY, STUDENTS, STAFF, AND ADMINISTRATORS ACTIVELY PARTICIPATE IN PROGRAM DESIGN, PROGRAM EXECUTION, DEVELOPMENT, DELIVERY AND ASSESSMENT. TO MEET THE EVER-EVOLVING NEEDS OF STAKEHOLDERS IN THE AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES COMMUNITIES, FREQUENT INTERACTIONS WITH STAKEHOLDER GROUPS WILL ENSURE RELEVANCE IN NEW AND EMERGING PROGRAMMING AREAS ADDRESSING THOSE NEEDS AND MAINTAIN FLEXIBILITY TO ALTER PLANS AS SITUATIONS ARISE. INCREASED USE OF TOOLS, SUCH AS A I, SOCIAL MEDIA, TELEVISION, FIELD DAYS, PASTURE WALKS; ALL WILL INCREASE PUBLIC AWARENESS AND MARKET PENETRATION OF THESE FAR-REACHING PROGRAMS. OHER VENUES ALONG WITH INCREASED FUNDING WILL ALLOW MORE FOCUSED AND CURRENT NEEDS TO BE ADDRESSED AT THE FARM, HOME AND SOCIETY LEVEL. THE SU AG CENTER WILL CONTINUE TO ENSURE RESOURCES ARE AVAILABLE AND APPROPRIATELY ALLOCATED TO ADDRESS THOSE MOST CRITICAL AND AREAS OF AGRICULTURE, HEALTH AND NUTRITION OF THE CONSUMING PUBLIC AND BE FLEXIBLE TO ALTER PLANS AS SITUATION ARISE.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE USDA'S NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE (NIFA) IS PARTNERING WITH SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CENTER (SUAREC) AND ITS 1890 CENTER OF EXCELLENCE FOR NUTRITION, WELLNESS, AND QUALITY OF LIFE (COE-NWQL) TO ESTABLISH THE FIRST USDA PILOT NUTRITION HUB. THE NEW HUB WILL CONTINUE THE WORK ON FOOD, NUTRITION, AND HEALTH-RELATED OUTCOMES IN AFRICAN AMERICAN COMMUNITIES.THIS ENDEAVOR IS ALIGNED WITH USDA STRATEGIC PLAN FY 2022-2026, INCLUDING GOAL 2: ENSURE AMERICA'S AGRICULTURAL SYSTEM IS EQUITABLE, RESILIENT, AND PROSPEROUS; AND GOAL 4: PROVIDE ALL AMERICANS SAFE, NUTRITIOUS FOOD. IT ALSO ALIGNS WITH STRATEGIC PRIORITIES OF SUAREC AND THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, HEALTH, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES.THE NUTRITION HUB WILL INTEGRATE AND COORDINATE THE COLLECTIVE WORK OF REE AGENCIES TO IMPROVE FOOD AND NUTRITION SECURITY AND REDUCE THE BURDEN OF DIET-RELATED CHRONIC DISEASES, ESPECIALLY IN UNDERSERVED, AT-RISK COMMUNITIES. FOUR MAIN GOALS ARE PROPOSED: (1) BUILD CURRENT AND FUTURE WORKFORCE CAPACITY FOR TRANS-DISCIPLINARY APPROACHES BETWEEN RESEARCH AND EXTENSION; (2) DEVELOP COLLABORATIONS AND PARTNERSHIPS WITH ORGANIZATIONS THAT SERVE THE AFRICAN AMERICAN COMMUNITIES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE REAL-WORLD OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES AROUND FOOD, NUTRITION, AND DIET-RELATED HEALTH DISPARITIES; (3) DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE SCIENCE-BASED NUTRITION INFORMATION AND CONNECT COMMUNITIES WITH FOOD AND NUTRITION SECURITY AND ECONOMIC VITALITY PROGRAMS; (4) FOSTER RESEARCH AND TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES IN HUMAN NUTRITION RESEARCH, PARTICULARLY IN UNDERSERVED AND UNDERREPRESENTED COMMUNITIES.THIS PARTNERSHIP WILL LEVERAGE RESOURCES FROM THE USDA-NIFA AND SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY TO ENSURE ALL GOALS AND PROPOSED ACTIVITIES ARE ACHIEVED AND MAKE THE INTENDED IMPACT ON THE TARGET STAKEHOLDERS.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** TO INCREASE PROFIT MARGINS WITHIN THEIR COMPANIES, SMALL FARMERS ARE INQUIRING ABOUT PROVIDING MEAT HARVESTING SERVICES. TO SUPPORT THEIR MOBILE LIVESTOCK HARVESTING UNIT, THE SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH DEPARTMENT HAS A HARVESTING HOUSE ON THE BATON ROUGE CAMPUS. CURRENTLY, THE USDA HAS IDENTIFIED A NEED FOR MORE USDA-CERTIFIED PROCESSING LOCATIONS IN THE UNITED STATES. IN LOUISIANA, FARMERS ARE FORCED TO TRAVEL TO NEIGHBORING STATES TO PROCESS THEIR LIVESTOCK, INCREASING THE COST OF PROCESSING. THERE IS ALSO A LACK OF KNOWLEDGEABLE PROCESSORS IN THE STATE, WHICH CREATES AN OPPORTUNITY TO TRAIN A STABLE WORKFORCE OF NEW PROCESSORS. IN RESEARCHING THE VIABILITY OF THE USEFULNESS OF THE UNIT, TWO UNIVERSITIES OPERATE MOBILE LIVESTOCK HARVESTING. THE THREE KNOWN UNIVERSITIES THAT OPERATE A MOBILE HARVESTING LAB/UNIT ARE KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY, DELAWARE STATE UNIVERSITY, AND VIRGINIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION. THE SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CENTER'S (SUAREC) INSTITUTIONAL STRATEGIC PLAN GOAL IS TO WORK WITH STAKEHOLDERS REPRESENTING FEDERAL, STATE, AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, AS WELL AS PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ORGANIZATIONS, TO PREPARE TRADITIONALLY UNSERVED AND UNDERSERVED RANCHERS, WOMEN, VETERANS, AND SMALL FARMERS TO PRODUCE AND COMPETE IN A CHANGING AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY. SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL AND EXTENSION CENTER COVERS SOME OF THE 64 PARISHES OF THE STATE. IN LOUISIANA, THERE ARE CURRENTLY 43,798 FARMERS, AND OF THAT TOTAL, 3,126 ARE AFRICAN AMERICAN, 15,345 ARE WOMEN, 13,097 ARE BEGINNERS, AND 4,751 ARE MILITARY SERVICE. (CENSUS, 2017) AGRICULTURE HAS ALWAYS BEEN ONE OF THE TOP INDUSTRIES IN LOUISIANA, AND MOST PARTICIPANTS RAISE LIVESTOCK AS A PROFESSION.THE SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CENTER HAS A STATE-CERTIFIED MEAT PROCESSING LAB ON CAMPUS. THE BUILDING IS USED TO EDUCATE STUDENTS IN THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES PROGRAM ABOUT THE SAFE HANDLING OF LIVESTOCK, ALONG WITH PROPER PROCEDURES IN THE HARVESTING PROCESS. THE EXTENSION DEPARTMENT OF THE AGRICULTURAL CENTER WILL PROVIDE TRAINING AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT TO FARMERS ACROSS THE STATE OF LOUISIANA. THE LIVESTOCK HARVESTING UNIT WILL PROVIDE HARVESTING OF BEEF CATTLE, SHEEP, GOATS, AND PIGS TO FARMERS/RANCHERS WHO NEED SERVICES IN RURAL COMMUNITIES THAT DO NOT HAVE OR ARE NOT ABLE TO TRAVEL TO A FACILITY ELSEWHERE IN THE STATE. THIS WILL HELP INCREASE THE PROFITABILITY OF NEW, BEGINNING RANCHERS, AND TRADITIONALLY UNSERVED AND UNDERSERVED WOMEN, VETERAN, AND SMALL FARMERS IN LOUISIANA. VIRGINIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION OPERATES A MOBILE PROCESSING UNIT THAT HAS BEEN SERVICING ITS CONSTITUENTS SINCE 2015. SOUTHERN WILL ADAPT THIS PROGRAM AFTER THE SUCCESS OF VIRGINIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** RIPE ROT CAUSED BY COLLETOTRICHUM SPP. OFTEN CAUSES HUGE ECONOMIC LOSSES IN THE HUMID SUBTROPICAL AND TROPICAL REGIONS BECAUSE OF ITS BROAD HOST RANGE, AND THE DEVASTATION OF ESSENTIAL CROPS.IN THIS PROJECT, WE PROPOSE TO USE ADVANCES IN SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGY AND AVAILABLE GERMPLASM RESOURCES TO UNDERSTAND RIPE ROT TOLERANCE USING GRAPE AS A MODEL PLANT. THE MAJOR OBJECTIVES OF THE PROJECT ARE: (I) TO IDENTIFY THE SPECIES DYNAMICS AND DISTRIBUTION OF GRAPE RIPE ROT, (II) MONITOR GLOBAL TRANSCRIPTOME PROFILE IN RIPE ROT SUSCEPTIBLE AND TOLERANT GRAPEVINES, (III) PHENOTYPING AND GENOTYPING TO IDENTIFY GENETIC VARIANTS AND DEVELOP GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION MAPS (GWAS) FOR RIPE ROT RESISTANCE, AND (IV) ENGAGE 1890 STUDENTS IN RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES WITH MODERN PLANT BREEDING TECHNIQUES. KNOWLEDGE WILL BE TRANSFERRED VIA SUAREC EXTENSION ACTIVITIES, PUBLICATIONS, PRESENTATIONS, AND FIELD TOURS.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CENTER (SUAREC) PROVIDES AGRICULTURAL TRAINING TO INCARCERATED, ADUDICATED AND HOMELESS YOUTH. THREE SITES ARE IDENTIFIED AND HAVE CAMPUS GARDENS, THRIVE ACADEMY, YOUTH OASIS AND AMI KIDS. THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO MODIFY THE APPLICATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE GARDENING PROJECT BY ADDRESSING THE COMPONENTS OF NUTRITION EDUCATION, INTERPERSONAL SOCIAL SKILLS, AND WORK SKILLS TO CREATE OPPORTUNITIES FOR ADJUDICATED, INCARCERATED AND HOMELESS YOUTH. OBJECTIVES INCLUDE (1) TO DEVELOP A GARDEN PROGRAM AND THERAPEUTIC HORTICULTURE EXPERIENCE FOR ADJUDICATED AND INCARCERATED YOUTH WITHIN THE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY AND SCHOOL CAMPUS; AND (2) TO PROMOTE HEALTHY LIFESTYLES THROUGH NUTRITION EDUCATION TO ADJUDICATED AND INCARCERATED YOUTH; AND (3) TO PROVIDE ADJUDICATED AND INCARCERATED YOUTH WITH INTERPERSONAL AND PROFESSIONAL WORK SKILLS FOR CAREER OPPORTUNITIES AND FAMILY STRENGTHENING TECHNIQUES. INSTRUCTION INVOLVES BOTH CLASSROOM AND HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES INCLUDING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF HORTICULTURAL GARDEN PLOTS. CERTIFICATES ARE AWARDED UPON SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE PROGRAM; THEY CAN BE UTILIZED TO SUPPORT EMPLOYMENT APPLICATIONS AT ANY HORTICULTURALLY-RELATED ESTABLISHMENT. THE MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH TO THIS PROJECT WILL ALLOW YOUTH PARTICIPANTS TO GAIN HORTICULTURAL AND NUTRITIONAL KNOWLEDGE, INTERPERSONAL SOCIAL SKILLS, AND WORK SKILLS TO BETTER PREPARE THEM FOR A HEALTHY AND PRODUCTIVE LIFESTYLE UPON RELEASE AND ULTIMATELY REDUCE RECIDIVISM.

THE SCOPE OF THIS PROJECT ALIGNS DIRECTLY WITH SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CENTER'S (SUAREC) LONG-RANGE GOALS. THESE INCLUDE DELIVERING: A) NEW RESEARCH-BASED TECHNOLOGIES; B) QUALITY AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION PROGRAMS; C) SERVICES TO IMPROVE ECONOMIC CONDITIONS; AND D) QUALITY OF LIFE FOR LIMITED-RESOURCE FARMERS WHILE BUILDING RESEARCH CAPACITY IN PLANT-BASED NUTRACEUTICAL RESEARCH. SUAREC IN COLLABORATION WITH USDA AND GRAPE GROWERS WILL USE BIOSTIMULATOR AND LEDS TO ENHANCE THE PHYTO-NUTRACEUTICALS IN GRAPES FOR INCREASING THEIR ANTIOXIDANT CAPACITY AND SUBSEQUENTLY ENHANCE THEIR HUMAN HEALTH BENEFITS. THE MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH APPROACH INCLUDES: (I) APPLICATION OF BIOSTIMULATOR/STIMULANTS TO RIPENING AND RIPE MUSCADINE BERRIES; (II) DETERMINING CHANGES IN GENE EXPRESSION ASSOCIATED WITH FLAVONOID/STILBENOID SYNTHESIS; (III) ELUCIDATE THE EFFECT OF BERRY EXTRACTS ON INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES AND STUDY THE PROFILE/ACTIVITY OF PROTEASOME VARIANTS AND AUTOPHAGY MECHANISM IN LUNG PRIMARY AND ADENOCARCINOMA EPITHELIAL CELLS; AND (IV) DEVELOP LEADERSHIP AND TECHNICAL SKILLS OF MINORITY STUDENTS IN AGRICULTURE/ CANCER/MOLECULAR BIOLOGY RESEARCH. IN BRIEF, WE WILL USE NATURALLY OCCURRING BIOSTIMULATOR MELATONIN AND EMERGING LED LIGHTING TECHNOLOGY TO ENRICH GRAPE NUTRACEUTICAL COMPOUNDS WITH AIM TO DEVELOP PRODUCTS WITH IMPROVED HEALTH BENEFITS. OUR FINDINGS WILL ENHANCE SCIENCE-BASED KNOWLEDGE AND WILL SUPPORT THE TRAINING OF UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS IN CHROMATOGRAPHY, MASS SPECTROMETRY, ANIMAL CELL CULTURES AND GENE EXPRESSION/ACTIVATION STUDIES. THE KNOWLEDGE GAINED WILL EXPAND OUR IDEAS ABOUT THE APPLICATION OF BIOSTIMULATORS/LED TECHNOLOGY TO OTHER SMALL FRUITS AND NICHE CROPS THAT WILL INCREASE THEIR UTILIZATION AND MARKET VALUE. THE ACQUIRED RESEARCH EXPERIENCES AND COLLABORATION WILL STRENGTHEN SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY RESEARCH CAPABILITIES AND COMPETITIVENESS.

THE CURRENT PLAN OF WORK FOR FY 2018-2022 SUBMITTED HEREIN IS BASED ON THE COLLECTIVE INPUTS OF STUDENTS, FACULTY, STAFF AND ADMINISTRATORS REPRESENTING RESEARCH, INSTRUCTIONAL AND COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAMS. THEIR INPUTS WERE BASED ON THE PRESSING NEEDS OF STUDENTS AND ALSO THE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION AGENDA AS INFLUENCED BY DIVERSE STAKEHOLDERS. SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY EXPERIENCED DEEP REDUCTIONS IN STATE BUDGETS FROM 2008 TO 2016 LEAVING THE INSTITUTION WITH LITTLE OR NO FUNDS FOR BUILDING CONSTRUCTION AND MAINTENANCE. SIMULTANEOUSLY, CLASS SIZES INCREASED AND THE NEEDS OF LOUISIANA CITIZENS ESCALATED PARTLY DUE TO NATURAL DISASTERS (HURRICANE, FLOOD, OIL SPILL, ETC.). TO ADEQUATELY ADDRESS THESE NEW NEEDS AND TO RETAIN TECHNOLOGY SAVVY STUDENTS, FACULTY AND STAFF, WE PLAN TO CONSTRUCT A MULTI-PURPOSE/MULTI-PROGRAM AGRICULTURAL LIVESTOCK COMPLEX. THIS FACILITY WILL BE UTILIZED BY THE THREE PROGRAMS - RESEARCH, INSTRUCTIONAL AND COOPERATIVE EXTENSION. IT WILL BE ACCESSIBLE AND BENEFICIAL TO STUDENTS, FACULTY, STAFF, CLIENTELE AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS. IT IS ALSO OUR INTENT TO REPLACE OLD AND OBSOLETE EQUIPMENT BY REBUILDING BOTH THE FOOD AND NUTRITION ANALYTICAL LABORATORY HOUSED IN A. O. WILLIAMS, THE SEWING AND SKILLS TRANSFER LABORATORY IN PINKIE THRIFT HALL AND ACQUIRING NEW VEHICLES ESPECIALLY 7-SEATER PASSENGER VANS. THE DEPARTMENT OF FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES OFFERS THE BACHELOR OF SCIENCE DEGREE IN FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES WITH CONCENTRATIONS IN APPAREL MERCHANDISING AND TEXTILES, CHILD DEVELOPMENT, AND HUMAN NUTRITION AND FOOD. solicitations.title: PURPOSE:  TECHNICAL ABSTRACT THE EARTHS UPPER ATMOSPHERE VARIES ON SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL SCALES AND THIS VARIATION CAN HAVE ADVERSE EFFECTS ON OPERATIONAL SYSTEMS. TO REDUCE THE RISKS FROM UNCERTAINTIES IN THESE SYSTEMS, WE ARE BUILDING, TESTING, AND DEMONSTRATING AN INSTRUMENT THAT WILL PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT THE STATE OF THE ATMOSPHERE DURING AND AFTER LARGE GEOMAGNETIC STORMS. OUR SENSOR, CALLED NOMAD, WILL REMOTELY OBSERVE NITRIC OXIDE (NO) THAT IS A MINOR SPECIES PRODUCED DURING STORMS. NO LEADS TO EFFICIENT COOLING AND COLLAPSE OF THE ATMOSPHERE, THUS REDUCING DENSITIES THAT AFFECTS DEBRIS COLLISION ASSESSMENT. THIS WORK BUILDS A SENSOR TO OBSERVE NO AND WILL BE HOSTED ON A STRATOSPHERIC DRONE AT 20 KM FOR CONTINUOUS MONITORING FOR EXTENDED PERIODS. WE WILL FINALIZE OUR DESIGN, DEVELOP, AND TEST NOMAD IN PHASE II, INTEGRATE IT INTO ARGOS, AND DEVELOP/TEST THE DATA COLLECTION/PROCESSING SYSTEM. THREE UNITS WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO OUR ARGOS AIRCRAFT WITH THREE VIEWING ANGLES TO OBSERVE NO DYNAMICS IN A 200300 KM REGION ABOVE ARGOS. THIS WORK EXPANDS OBSERVATIONAL TOOLS THAT SUPPORT SHORT- AND LONG-TERM SPACE WEATHER PREDICTIONS AND WILL PROVIDE DECISION MAKERS WITH IMPROVED CHARACTERIZATION AND PREDICTION OF THE TIMING, INTENSITY, AND IMPACT OF STORM SPACE WEATHER EVENTS ON CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE.  SUMMARY OF THE ANTICIPATED RESULTS AND IMPLICATIONS OF THE APPROACH AND THE POTENTIAL COMMERCIAL APPLICATIONS OF THE RESEARCH FOR A FRACTION OF SATELLITE DEPLOYMENT AND OPERATIONS COST AND FOR BETTER TEMPORAL AND SPATIAL RESOLUTION, AGENCY OPERATORS OF SPACE TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS WILL BE ABLE TO SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASE THEIR CURRENT EPOCH AND FORECAST ACCURACY OF THERMOSPHERIC DENSITIES TO REDUCE THE HAZARD FROM DEBRIS COLLISIONS. NOMAD WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT NOAAS MISSION TO DEVELOP A SPACE TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT SYSTEM THROUGH THE OFFICE OF SPACE COMMERCE TRAFFIC COORDINATION SYSTEM FOR SPACE PROGRAM. THE TRACSS PROGRAM WILL USE DATA ASSIMILATIVE MODELING TO PRODUCE IMPROVED WEATHER OF THERMOSPHERE DENSITIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A NO SENSOR ON A HIGH-ALTITUDE UAV PLATFORM FOR THE PURPOSE OF CREATING A 24/7 OPERATIONAL DATA STREAM OF REMOTELY SENSED LOWER THERMOSPHERIC NO. THE NO ABOVE ARGOS IS PRODUCED DURING AND AFTER GEOMAGNETIC STORMS AND THE OBSERVATIONS OF IT CAN FEED THERMOSPHERIC DENSITY MODELS. SET ANTICIPATES REVENUE GENERATION FROM THREE STREAMS: I) PAYLOAD HOSTING THROUGH NASA AND OTHER AGENCIES TO SUPPORT FLEET EXPANSION; II) EQUIPMENT LEASING TO AGENCIES TO SUPPORT OPERATIONAL EXPANSION; AND III) DATA AS A SERVICE TO AGENCIES WORKING TO IMPROVE SPACE DOMAIN AWARENESS AND SPACE TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT. WE DO INTEND TO INITIALLY HOST OTHER, NON-NOMAD DATA, INCLUDING RADIATION DATA FOR AVIATION, GNSS TEC, AND D-REGION ABSORPTION.

COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH: VINES: TRACK 2: SEA-NET: SCALABLE EDGE ANALYTICS AND NETWORKING FOR AUTONOMOUS MARITIME EMERGENCY RESPONSE -MARITIME EMERGENCY RESPONSE RELIES ON SLOW AND MANUAL COORDINATION, LEADING TO CRITICAL DELAYS DURING CRISES. SINCE TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS FAIL OFFSHORE, RELIABLE BROADBAND IS ESSENTIAL FOR VESSEL SAFETY. THIS PROJECT SERVES THE U.S. NATIONAL INTEREST BY DEVELOPING A RESILIENT COMMUNICATION AND EDGE COMPUTING SYSTEM FOR AUTONOMOUS MARITIME INTELLIGENCE. BY ENABLING FASTER DISASTER RESPONSE, IT SEEKS TO SAVE THOUSANDS OF LIVES AND BILLIONS OF DOLLARS ANNUALLY. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE AMERICAN WORKFORCE BY PROVIDING STUDENTS AND EARLY-CAREER RESEARCHERS WITH HANDS-ON TRAINING IN HIGH-IMPACT EXPERIMENTATION AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI). THE DELIVERABLES FROM THIS PROJECT DIRECTLY IMPACT THE EVOLUTION OF 6G BY PIONEERING AI-NATIVE ARCHITECTURES THAT MOVE BEYOND 5G'S BIT-CENTRIC LIMITATIONS. THE PROJECT GOAL IS TO DEMONSTRATE AUTONOMOUS MARITIME OPERATIONS BY INTEGRATING NEXT-GENERATION NETWORKS, EDGE COMPUTING, AND AI MODELS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DYNAMICALLY ORCHESTRATE WIRELESS SPECTRUM ACROSS HETEROGENEOUS PLATFORMS LIKE UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES (UAVS) AND SURFACE VESSELS. TECHNICAL METHODS INCLUDE HIERARCHICAL SEMANTIC ENCODING AND AGE OF INFORMATION-BASED SCHEDULING TO ENSURE DATA FRESHNESS FOR REAL-TIME EDGE INFERENCE. SPECIFICALLY, SEMANTIC ENCODING COMPRESSES PAYLOADS DELIVERING A GOODPUT MORE THAN 90% OF THE REQUIRED SEMANTIC PAYLOAD SIZE, WHILE A SOFTWARE-DEFINED NETWORKING CONTROLLER ENSURES RESILIENT AND LOW-LATENCY (LESS THAN 50MS) HANDOVERS ACROSS AGGREGATED 5G AND SATELLITE LINKS. A CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROVENANCE FRAMEWORK, CALLED TRUSTEDBITS, IS INTRODUCED TO MAINTAIN DATA SECURITY IN DENIED, DEGRADED, INTERMITTENT, AND LIMITED (DDIL) ENVIRONMENTS. THE PROJECT ALSO INCORPORATES EXPLAINABLE AI MODELS TO PROVIDE TRANSPARENT RATIONALES FOR HUMAN-AI TEAMING, ENSURING A TIME-TO-ACTIONABLE DECISION OF UNDER 60 SECONDS. TECHNOLOGY VALIDATION INVOLVES HIGH-SPEED TOWING TANK TESTS AND AT-SCALE HUDSON RIVER DEMONSTRATIONS TO REDUCE INCIDENT RESPONSE TIME BY UP TO 30% COMPARED TO THE CURRENT MANUAL RESPONSE. THESE TRIALS WILL PROGRESSIVELY ADVANCE THE SYSTEM TO TECHNOLOGY READINESS LEVEL (TRL) 6. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.

DESCRIPTION:THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING TO THE STILLAGUAMISH TRIBE OF INDIANS, NATURAL RESOURCES DEPARTMENT, TO SUPPORT THE TRIBE'S WORK TO ADVANCE PUGET SOUND RECOVERY AND PROTECT TRIBAL TREATY RESOURCES THROUGH THE USE OF SMALL-UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEMS (SUAS) FOR ENVIRONMENTAL DATA COLLECTION, WILDLIFE MONITORING TO ASSESS CHINOOK PREDATION, AND ESTUARY RESTORATION ACTIONS. ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE ENGAGING IN OUTREACH AND EDUCATION, ADVANCING LARGE-SCALE HABITAT RESTORATION PROJECTS, MONITORING RIPARIAN VEGETATION HEALTH, PLAN FOR SHELLFISH RESILIENCY, AND IMPROVING THE USE AND ACCESSIBILITY OF DECADES OF DATA RELATED TO STILLAGUAMISH CHINOOK SALMON. TRIBAL STAFF WILL UTILIZE SUAS (SMALL-UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEMS) AND HIGH-RESOLUTION MAPPING TO PERFORM A SYSTEMATIC INVENTORY OF TRIBALLY OWNED PARCELS DESIGNATED FOR CONSERVATION AND RESTORATION PURPOSES, PRODUCING HIGH-RESOLUTION GEOREFERENCED ORTHOMOSAICS. THE TRIBE WILL ALSO BUILD OFF FROM PAST WORK IN CONTINUING TO MONITOR ESTUARINE WILDLIFE IN THE STILLAGUAMISH RIVER BASIN WHILE ACTIVELY PARTICIPATING IN REGIONAL MEETINGS, TO ENSURE THAT TRIBAL PERSPECTIVES ARE REPRESENTED IN PUGET SOUND RECOVERY INITIATIVES WHILE INCORPORATING RESULTS FROM THEIR RESEARCH AND OUTREACH.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE THE DOCUMENTATION OF UAS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL RESTORATION COURSE COMPLETION, AND SIX HIGH-RESOLUTION ORTHOMOSAIC MAPS, 440 DATASHEETS FROM AVIAN SURVEY EVENTS AND PRE AND POST RESTORATION SPECIES ASSEMBLAGES' COMPARISON; AND, FOUR SEASONAL DISTRIBUTION MAPS, ONE HAUL OUT MAP AND 25 SURVEY DATASHEETS FROM SEAL SURVEY EVENTS, DESIGNS, REPORTS, PERMIT APPLICATIONS, AND RELATED DOCUMENTS FOR LARGE RESTORATION PROJECTS IN THE STILLAGUAMISH WATERSHED, AN UPDATED QUALITY ASSURANCE PROJECT PLAN (QAPP), ANNUAL INTERTIDAL WORK PLANS, ANNUAL DRONE FLIGHTS FOR SEDIMENT MAP UPDATES, CONTINUOUS TEMPERATURE MONITORING, THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE A PATHWAY FOR SAFE, SUSTAINABLE, AND RESILIENT SHELLFISH POPULATIONS THAT WILL BENEFIT BOTH TRIBAL MEMBERSHIP AND THE HEALTH OF PUGET SOUND. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES ARE THE MEMBERS OF THE STILLAGUAMISH INDIAN TRIBE AND SURROUNDING COMMUNITIES.

THE EXTENSION AND OUTREACH COMPONENT OF TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY'S LAND-GRANT MISSION IS CARRIED OUT THROUGH THE COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM IN THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE. THE PROGRAM'S MISSION AND PURPOSE ARE TO PROVIDE RESEARCH-BASED, PRACTICAL INFORMATION TO TENNESSEE RESIDENTS THROUGH INFORMAL EDUCATION ACTIVITIES AIMED AT ENHANCING THE STATE'S SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL STRENGTHS. TSU EXTENSION PLACES A SPECIFIC EMPHASIS ON REACHING OUT TO ASSIST FARMERS AND PRODUCERS, WORKING COLLABORATIVELY WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE, THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, AND COUNTY GOVERNMENTS. TSU EXTENSION HAS A BROAD REACH, WITH COUNTY EXTENSION AGENTS/EDUCATORS, PROGRAM ASSISTANTS, AND SUPPORT STAFF IN 62 COUNTIES ACROSS THE STATE. THESE COUNTY PERSONNEL RECEIVE TRAINING AND EDUCATIONAL/TEACHING MATERIAL FROM TSU'S 23 CAMPUS-BASED EXTENSION FACULTY/SPECIALISTS. OUR PROGRAM IS ORGANIZED AROUND ADDRESSING CRITICAL ISSUES IN FOUR EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING AREAS: 1) AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES (ANR), WHICH ENHANCES URBAN AND RURAL PROSPERITY BY ASSISTING FARMERS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN PRODUCING FIELD CROPS, RAISING LIVESTOCK, MANAGING FORESTLANDS, GROWING FRUIT CROPS, AND TENDING HOME GARDENS, ACTIVITIES THAT PRODUCE FOOD AND ENHANCE THE ENVIRONMENTAL INTEGRITY OF THE AGROECOSYSTEM. THE ANR PROGRAM PROVIDES FARMERS WITH A WIDE VARIETY OF RESEARCH-BASED TRAINING PROGRAMS TO ENHANCE THEIR PRODUCTIVITY, FARM PROFITABILITY, AND QUALITY OF LIFE, FOCUSING ON ENTOMOLOGY, FORESTRY, SOIL HEALTH, BIOENERGY, PLANT NUTRITION, HORTICULTURE, DRONE TECHNOLOGY,  ECONOMICS, AGRICULTURAL COMMUNICATIONS, AND ORGANIC AGRICULTURE; 2) FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES, WHICH IMPROVES THE HEALTH AND WELL-BEING OF TENNESSEANS BY PROVIDING PROGRAMS ON COMMUNITY NUTRITION EDUCATION, NUTRITION SECURITY, FAMILY AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT, AND HEALTH EDUCATION; 3) EXTENSION 4-H YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, WHICH FOCUSES ON WORKFORCE PREPARATION, STEM EDUCATION, LIFE SKILLS DEVELOPMENT, YOUTH LEADERSHIP, CITIZENSHIP DEVELOPMENT, AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS; AND 4) COMMUNITY RESOURCES AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, WHICH PROVIDES INFORMATION AND EDUCATION ON COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT AND INCLUDES AGRIBUSINESS/ENTREPRENEURSHIP TRAINING FOR FARMERS (MANAGEMENT, BASIC ACCOUNTING, ECONOMIC PRINCIPLES, BUDGETS, WHOLE-FARM PLANNING, LAND ACQUISITION, TAX MANAGEMENT) AS WELL AS TRAINING FOR LOCAL BUSINESSES (BUSINESS PLANNING, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, MODERN MARKETING AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT).

THE EXTENSION AND OUTREACH COMPONENT OF THE LAND-GRANT MISSION OF THE TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY IS CARRIED OUT THROUGH THE COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM, IN THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE. THE MISSION AND PURPOSE OF THE COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM IS TO PROVIDE RES EARCH-BASED, USEFUL, AND PRACTICAL INFORMATION TO THE RESIDENTS OF TENNESSEE, THROUGH INFORMAL EDUCATION TO IMPROVE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. TSU'S COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM PUTS EXTRA EFFORT TO REACH OUT TO THE LIMITED-RESOURCE FARMERS, PRODUCERS, AND OTHERS IN THE STATE OF TENNESSEE. AND THE PROGRAM WORKS COLLABORATIVELY WITH UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE, THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, AND THE COUNTY GOVERNMENTS. TSU EXTENSION HAS COUNTY EXTENSION AGENTS/EDUCATORS, PROGRAM ASSISTANTS, AND SUPPORT STAFF IN 60 COUNTIES ACROSS THE STATE. OUR COUNTY PERSONNEL RECEIVE THEIR TRAINING AND EDUCATIONAL/TEACHING MATERIAL FROM THE 20 CAMPUS-BASED EXTENSION FACULTY/SPECIALISTS. COOPERATIVE EXTENSION AT TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY IS ORGANIZED TO ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES IN FOUR EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING CATEGORIES. I. AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES (ANR) THE AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES (ANR) PROGRAMS FOCUSES ON ASSISTING FARMERS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN GROWING FIELD CROPS OR HOME GARDENS TO PRODUCE FOOD AND ENHANCE ENVIRONMENTAL INTEGRITY OF THE AGROECOSYSTEM. THIS PROGRAM PROVIDES A WIDE VARIETY OF RESEARCHBASED TRAINING PROGRAMS TO FARMERS TO ENHANCE THEIR PRODUCTIVITY, FARM PROFITABILITY, AND QUALITY OF LIFE. THE KEY COMPONENTS OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE ENTOMOLOGY, PLANT PATHOLOGY, SOIL HEALTH, BIOENERGY, PLANT NUTRITION, HORTICULTURE, DRONE TECHNOLOGY, ECONOMICS, AGRICULTURAL COMMUNICATIONS AND ORGANIC AGRICULTURE. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE ANR PROGRAM IS TO ENHANCE THE RURAL PROSPERITY. II. FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES (FCS) FAMILY CONSUMER SCIENCE PROGRAM FOCUSES ON COMMUNITY NUTRITION EDUCATION, NUTRITION SECURITY, FAMILY AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT AND HEALTH EDUCATION THROUGH THE EXTENSION AGENTS AND CAMPUS BASED FACULTY WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF IMPROVING HEALTH AND WELLBEING OF THE POPULATION. III. EXTENSION 4-H YOUTH DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM THE 4-H AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOCUSES ON WORKFORCE PREPARATION, STEM EDUCATION, LIFE SKILLS DEVELOPMENT, YOUTH LEADERSHIP AND CITIZENSHIP DEVELOPMENT AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS. IV. COMMUNITY RESOURCES AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT: THE FOCUS OF THIS PROGRAM IS TO PROVIDE INFORMATION AND EDUCATION ON COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT. TO ACHIEVE THIS OBJECTIVE, TSU EXTENSION PROGRAM PROVIDES AGRIBUSINESS AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP TRAINING TO FARMERS. THE TRAINING INCLUDES TOPICS ON MANAGEMENT, BASIC ACCOUNTING, ECONOMIC PRINCIPLES, BUDGETS, WHOLE-FARM PLANNING, LAND ACQUISITION, TAX MANAGEMENT, AND WHOLE FARM PLANNING. THE PROGRAM ALSO PROVIDES TRAINING TO LOCAL BUSINESSES ON BUSINESS PLANNING, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, MODERN MARKETING AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT.

THROUGH THE INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH, THE GOAL OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AT TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY IS TO CREATE AND COMMUNICATE NEW KNOWLEDGE IN THE AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES. THROUGH OUR INNOVATIVE RESEARCH, WE ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF HUMANKIND, FOCUSING ON FINDING SOLUTIONS TO CHALLENGES FACED BY SOCIALLY AND ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED GROUPS, AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE PROSPERITY OF THE CITIZENS OF TENNESSEE, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. RESEARCH IN TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURE IS ORGANIZED TO ADDRESS THE CRITICAL ISSUES DESCRIBED BELOW. ENHANCING BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY SAFEGUARDING AND ENHANCING THE NATURAL RESOURCE ENVIRONMENT HAS BECOME INCREASINGLY COMPLEX WITHIN ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, RESOURCE AND PERSONAL CONTEXTS. THROUGH COLLABORATION AMONG RESEARCHERS, INDUSTRY, PRODUCERS, ENVIRONMENTAL GROUPS, AND GOVERNMENT, WE ARE HELPING PRESERVE A DIVERSE AND RESILIENT ENVIRONMENT FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. ENRICHING OUR ECONOMY HELPING FARMS AND AGRICULTURE BUSINESSES BECOME MORE PROFITABLE AND INDIVIDUALS BECOME FINANCIALLY SECURE BOOSTS THE LOCAL, STATE, AND NATIONAL ECONOMIES. OUR PROGRAMS STRIVE TO STRENGTHEN THE ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF ALL FACETS OF AGRIBUSINESS, AND IMPROVE THE FINANCIAL LITERACY OF TENNESSEANS AND BEYOND SO THEY MAY BUILD AND PROTECT WEALTH FOR THEMSELVES AND FUTURE GENERATIONS. STRENGTHENING OUR HEALTH MAKING HEALTHY CHOICES IS IMPORTANT FOR HUMANS, ANIMALS, AND EVEN OUR PLANET. AS A LEADER IN NUTRITION, ANIMAL WELFARE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, WE ARE WORKING TO UNDERSTAND HOW FOOD, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND SOCIAL CONNECTIONS AFFECT OVERALL HEALTH. FROM FOOD SAFETY TO DISEASE PREVENTION AND MAINTENANCE TO THE STATE OF OUR ENVIRONMENT, THESE EFFORTS WILL HELP AMERICANS AND THE REST OF THE WORLD LEAD HEALTHIER LIVES FOR GENERATIONS TO COME. SUPPORTING FOOD, FIBER, AND ENERGY SYSTEMS SAFE, SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS THAT ARE SOCIALLY, ECONOMICALLY, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY RESPONSIBLE ARE KEY TO ENHANCING THE LIVES OF TENNESSEANS AND SUPPORTING A GROWING GLOBAL POPULATION. WE ARE EXPLORING WAYS TO DELIVER DISCOVERIES USING A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO AGRICULTURE PRODUCTIVITY THAT WILL PROVIDE CUSTOMIZABLE SOLUTIONS FOR PRODUCERS. UTILIZING FACULTY IN THE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES AND THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SCIENCES, OUR RESE ARCH ADDRESSES THESE CRITICAL ISSUES THROUGH FACULTY GROUPS IN THE PLANT, ANIMAL, FOOD, AND HUMAN SCIENCES. THESE FACULTY-LED GROUPS FACILITATE THE IDENTIFICATION OF RESEARCH PRIORITIES WITHIN OUR CRITICAL ISSUES THAT ARE OF IMPORTANCE TO STAKEHOLDER GROUPS. WE CONDUCT RESEARCH IN AGRICULTURAL LEADERSHIP, EDUCATION AND COMMUNICATION THAT BRIDGES THE GAP BETWEEN THE GENERAL PUBLIC AND SCIE NTISTS WORKING TO SOLVE CURRENT AND EMERGING CHALLENGES RELATED TO SUSTAINABLY FEEDING AN EVER-GROWING POPULATION UNDER VARIOUS ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIETAL COMPLICATIONS. THIS RESEARCH ALSO BUILDS HUMAN AND INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITYNEEDED BY A VARIETY OF PUBLIC, PRIVATE, AND NONPROFIT EMPLOYERS IN THE AGRICULTURE SECTOR. ALSO STUDIED ARE WAYS TO DEVELOP HUMAN CAPACITY AND PROVIDE LEADERSHIP WITHIN COMMUNITIES. MUCH RESEARCH IN THIS AREA ALSO IDENTIFIES THE IMPACT OF TECHNOLOGY IN AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION, TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS LECTURE-CAPTURE, DRONES, ROBOTS, EXTENDED REALITY, AND 360-DEGREE VIDEO. IN THE AREA OF AGRIBUSINESS, WE HAVE STRONG APPLIED-RESEARCH COMPONENT. WE PREPARE STUDENTS, FARMERS, AND STAKEHOLDERS IN THE USE OF ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND MANAGEMENT COMPETENCIES TO TAKE ON THE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES OF A DYNAMIC AGRI-FOOD SYSTEM. THE RESEARCH AREA EMPHASIZES PROMOTING, DEVELOPING, AND IMPROVING THE UTILIZATION OF RESEARCH, OUTREACH CAPABILITIES AND OPPORTUNITIES INVOLVING AGRIBUSINESSES, NATURAL RESOURCES AND COMMUNITIES. MAIN ACTIVITIES INCLUDE INVESTIGATIONS ON THE SOLE OR COMBINATION OF STRATEGIES FOR PROFITABILITY, AND THE SUSTAINABILITY, SURVIVAL, EFFICIENCY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF AGRICULTURALOPERATIONS, PARTICULARLY SMALL FARM OPERATIONS. ANTICIPATED RESULTS INCLUDE FARMERS' ADOPTION OF NEW CROPS; INVESTMENT FOR ALTERNATE INCOME DIVERSIFICATION STRATEGIES SUCH AS AGRITOURISM; ENHANCED KNOWLEDGE ON BENEFITS AND COSTS OF SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES; IMPROVED FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT AND MARKETING STRATEGIES AND DEVELOPMENT OF ENTREPRENEURSHIP SKILLS. RESEARCH IN ANIMAL SCIENCE IS DIRECTED AT IMPROVING LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION SYSTEMS BY GENERATING NOVEL FINDINGS THAT IMPACT ANIMAL WELL-BEING AND PERFORMANCE. SUB-DISCIPLINES SUCH AS GENETICS, HEALTH, NUTRITION, AND REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY ARE INTEGRATED IN THE POULTRY AND RUMINANT LIVESTOCK RESEARCH ENDEAVORS. RESEARCH SPANS FROM BASIC, MOLECULAR MODELS TO APPLIED, WHOLE-ANIMAL SYSTEMS. PRIMARY END-USERS OF THE RESEARCH FINDINGS ARE LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS THAT ARE OFTEN SOCIALLY-DISADVANTAGED, RESOURCE-LIMITED OWNER-OPERATORS OF SMALL-SCALE ENTERPRISES. WE HAVE RESEARCH EFFORTS DIRECTED AT ELUCIDATING, MOLECULARLY AND FUNCTIONALLY, ANIMAL IMMUNE AND METABOLIC GENES. IN PARTICULAR, THOSE GENES THAT HAVE ANTIMICROBIAL ACTIVITIES AND THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL. WE ARE USING COMBINED APPROACHES OF BIOINFORMATICS, GENETICS AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY TO ELUCIDATE GENES OR GENE FAMILIES THAT ARE POTENTIALLY IMPORTANT IN ANIMAL HEALTH. SOME OF OUR ANIMAL PRODUCTION RESEARCH EMPHASIZES GOAT PRODUCTION. PROJECTS HAVE FOCUSED ON EVALUATING BREEDS TO GENERATE RECOMMENDATIONS ON HOW TO BEST USE THE DIFFERENT BREEDS FOR ENHANCED COMMERCIAL MEAT GOAT PRODUCTION. PRODUCERS HAVE MODIFIED THEIR GENETIC MANAGEMENT DECISION-MAKING LEADING TO IMPROVED HERD HEALTH, PERFORMANCE, AND ECONOMIC RETURN. IN POULTRY RESEARCH, THE CURRENT DEMAND FOR POULTRY AND POULTRY PRODUCTS REQUIRES A GAIN IN GENETIC POTENTIAL COMPLEMENTED WITH NUTRITIONAL REGIMENS THAT MAXIMIZE GROWTH AND IMPROVE EFFICIENCY OF FEED UTILIZATION. EXAMINATION OF OPTIMAL FEED COMPOSITION AND ALLOCATION IS OPTIMIZING SPECIFIC AMINO ACID CONCENTRATIONS. FEEDING THESE NEW LEVELS OF AMINO ACIDS WILLREDUCE FEEDING COST IN GUINEA FOWL PRODUCTION. OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE PREVENTION IS ADDRESSED IN A PROGRAM THAT FOCUSES ON DEVELOPING A SMARTPHONE APPLICATION FOR WIC FAMILIES THAT WILL PROVIDE TOOLS TO MAKE USING THEIR BENEFITS EASIER WHILE PROVIDING HEALTHY RECIPES, NUTRITION EDUCATION, AND A GOAL TRACKING TOOL. HEALTHY EATING EXTENDS BEYOND LIMITING INTAKE OF FATS AND CALORIES. OUR NUTRITION RESEARCH IS AIMED AT UNDERSTANDING THE EFFECTS AND MECHANISMS OF FOOD-DERIVED BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS AND THEIR ROLE IN COMBATING HUMAN CHRONIC DISEASES SUCH CANCER, OBESITY, AND DIABETES. RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE DIRECT EVIDENCE THAT HUMAN CHRONIC DISEASE CAN BE PREVENTED OR TREATED BY SELECTING FOODS HAVING HIGH LEVELS OF BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS. FOOD IS A CORNERSTONE OF HUMAN EXISTENCE. ONGOING FOOD SCIENCE RESEARCH FOCUSES ON IMPROVING THE SAFETY, QUALITY, SHELF-LIFE, NUTRIENT PROFILE AND SENSORY ATTRIBUTES OF NOVEL FOOD INGREDIENTS, DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING ADVANCED AND INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES FOR FOOD PROCESSING, MANUFACTURING, PACKAGING, AND SANITATION TO EFFECTIVELY REDUCE THE PRESENCE OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS. ALSO, WE ARE DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING NOVEL STRATEGIES FOR THE EFFECTIVE CONTROL OF PERSISTENT RESERVOIRS OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS AND MITIGATING ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE ACROSS THE FOOD CHAIN. FOR EXAMPLE, WE ARE LOOKING AT NEW WAYS TO REMOVE PATHOGENS FROM FOODS BY PRECISELY DEFINING THE LIMITS OF USING UV LIGHT AS A SUBSTITUTE FOR PASTEURIZATION TO ACHIEVE A SPECIFIED LETHALITY FOR DEADLY AGENTS IN FOODS. THIS PROCESS IS USING ADVANCED MATHEMATICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELS. TECHNIQUES DEVELOPED IN THIS PROGRAM ARE ALSO BEING INVESTIGATED FOR POSSIBLE APPLICATION TO CONTROL THE SPREAD OF SARS-COV-2 AND OTHER VIRUSES. OTHER FOOD SCIENCE RESEARCH IS ADDRESSING THE PROBLEM OF CAMPYLOBACTER. THIS ORGANISM IS ONE OF THE MOST COMMON CAUSES OF DIARRHEAL ILLNESS IN THE UNITED STATES. DUE TO THE PREVALENCE OF CAMPYLOBACTER IN RAW CHICKEN PRODUCTS, ROUTINE AND RELIABLE MONITORING IS NECESSARY TO REDUCE ITS IMPACT UPON HUMAN HEALTH. THE METHOD BEING DEVELOPED IS INTENDED TO BE USED BY FOOD INDUSTRY AND REGULATORY TESTING LABORATORIES TO FACILITATE IMPROVED IDENTIFICATION OF CAMPYLOBACTER IN PROCESSING FACILITIES AND FINAL PRODUCTS. TO MITIGATE THE SPREAD OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANT CONTAMINANTS IN FOODS, WE HAVE RESEARCH THAT HAS GENERATED A SERIES OF HOTSPOT MAPS THAT WILL BE USED IN WORKSHOPS/WEBINARS TO ILLUSTRATE ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANT BACTERIAL COMMUNITIES ON PRODUCER'S FARMS. BY USING PERSONALIZED HOTSPOT MAPS THAT DISPLAY THE FREQUENCY OF ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANT BACTERIA IN FARMS, PRODUCERS WILL MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ON THE USAGE OF ANTIBIOTICS IN THEIR LIVESTOCK, THUS REDUCING THE THREAT OF CONTAMINATION OF FOOD CROPS FERTILIZED WITH THE ANTIMICROBIAL-RESISTANT MANURE. RESEARCH IN NATURAL RESOURCES USES MULTIDISCIPLINE APPROACHES TO UNDERSTAND AND ATTENUATE PROBLEMS CAUSED BY CLIMATE CHANGE, LAND DE GRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, EMERGING CONTAMINANTS, AND ANTHROPOGENIC STRESSORS. TRADITIONAL AND CUTTING-EDGE CHEMISTRY METHODS ARE USED TO STUDY FATE OF CHEMICALS IN THE ENVIRONMENT, THE INTERACTION OF HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES WITH SOILS AND WATER AND BIOGEOCHEMICAL CYCLES. BIOTECHNOLOGY IS USED TO STUDY AND RECTIFY HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS, WILDLIFE DISEASES AND PARASITES, MONITOR RARE AND ENDANGERED SPECIES, AND SOIL HEALTH. GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS, REMOTE SENSING AND ADVANCED STATISTICS ARE USED TO MODEL CLIMATE CHANGE ON A LARGE SCALE, WILDLIFE ECOSYSTEMS, DETERMINE THE VALUE OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AND DOCUMENT WATER RESOURCES. OUR RESEARCH TAKES PLACE IN CHEMISTRY LABS, COMPUTER LABS, RURAL AND URBAN SETTINGS AS WE SEEK TO SUSTAIN AND IMPROVE THE NATION'S NATURAL RESOURCES. IN ADDITION TO RESEARCH, WE BUILD INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY AND STRENGTHEN OUR ENVIRONMENTAL PROGRAM THROUGH BRIDGE PROGRAMS, STUDENT RECRUITMENT AND MENTORING, STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS, AGGRESSIVE PROPOSAL WRITING AND CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT. THE GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A STRONG DIVERSE WORKFORCE IN THE NATURAL RESOURCES THAT REFLECTS OUR NATION'S DEMOGRAPHICS. PLANT SCIENCE RESEARCH INCLUDES DIVERSE FIELDS IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS WITH A FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AND APPLYING SCIENTIFIC AND BIOTECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES TO IMPROVE CROP PRODUCTIVITY, REDUCE LOSSES FROM DISEASE, INSECT PESTS, AND TOXIC METAL STRESS; IN ADDITION TO IMPROVING THE UNDERSTANDING OF PLANT STRESS TOLERANCE MECHANISMS FOR HANDLING HEAT, DROUGHT AND OTHER STRESS FACTORS. RESEARCH INCLUDES THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR IMPROVING THE PRODUCTION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT OF ALTERNATIVE PRODUCTS FOR REDUCING PESTICIDE INPUTS IN CROP PRODUCTION SYSTEMS SUCH AS MICROBIAL-BASED PRODUCTS, PHEROMONES, AND PLANT OILS, PLANT GENETIC RESISTANCE AND BY BROADENING SOYBEAN GENETIC DIVERSITY FOR FUTURE GAINS IN CROP PRODUCTIVITY AND PREPAREDNESS FOR EMERGING NEW DISEASES AND INSECT PESTS. CROPS ADDRESSED ARE DIVERSE, INCLUDING VEGETABLES, CORN, SOYBEANS, ORNAMENTAL NURSERY CROPS, BIOENERGY CROPS, HYDROPONICS, AND URBAN AGRICULTURE. TECHNOLOGICAL CONTRIBUTIONS FROM THIS RESEARCH INCLUDE INCREASING CROP DIVERSITY BY INTRODUCING NEW EXOTIC VEGETABLES AND AMARANTH, DEVELOPING NEW CROP ALTERNATIVES LIKE HEMP, AND BIOFUEL ALTERNATIVES SUCH AS PERENNIAL SWITCHGRASS AND WINTER CANOLA THAT HAVE IMPROVED DIGESTIBILITY AND PROCESSING, AND DEVELOPING NEW PLANTS TOLERANT TO HEAT STRESS. OTHER RESEARCH ACTIVITIES ON BEST CROP MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, NITROGEN APPLICATION RATES TO ENHANCE YIELD AND FEEDSTOCK CHARACTERISTICS, THE BEST WINTER CANOLA VARIETIES AND NITROGEN RATES FOR TENNESSEE DELIVER SERVICES OF VALUE TO SOCIETY. AN OVERALL LACK OF CROP DIVERSITY IN THE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS OF THE SOUTHEASTERN UNITED STATES INCREASES THE THREATS OF DISEASE EPIDEMICS, INSECT PEST OUTBREAKS OR RISKS OF CROP FAILURE DUE TO ABIOTIC STRESSES. IT IS IMPORTANT TO DEVELOP ALTERNATIVE CROPS FOR PRODUCTIVE SYSTEMS. RESEARCH TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE HAS PRODUCED THE RELEASE OF TWO GRAIN AMARANTH VARIETIES AND THE RELEASE OF TWO GRAIN LEGUME VARIETIES. THESE ALTERNATIVE CROPS GIVE PRODUCERS OPTIONS IN SELECTING PRODUCTION MARKETS. ANOTHER PROGRAM LEADING TO CROP DIVERSITY IS EXAMINING THE ROLE OF SWEET SORGHUM AS A POTENTIAL DEDICATED US BIOFUEL CROP. THIS PROGRAM IS ESTABLISHING INNOVATIVE PROTOCOLS FOR SWEET SORGHUM GENETIC ENHANCEMENT. AS MORE KNOWLEDGE IS GAINED ABOUT THE INTERCONNECTEDNESS OF HUMAN IMPACTS ON THE EARTH, THE ROLE OF ANTIBIOTIC CONTAMINATION ON SOIL HEALTH IS BEING EXAMINED. MICRONUTRIENT DEFICIENCY IS A MAJOR CONCERN IN THE PRODUCTION OF SOME CROPS, SOME OF OUR RESEARCH WILL SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE THE UNDERSTANDING THE BIOGEOCHEMICAL CYCLING OF MICRONUTRIENTS IN THE PRESENCE OF ANTIBIOTICS. THREATS FROM DISEASE AND INSECT PESTS ARE BEING ADDRESSED IN A NUMBER OF RESEARCH PROGRAMS. PLANT DISEASE IS A MAJOR THREAT TO GLOBAL FOOD PRODUCTION COSTING THE US ECONOMY AN ESTIMATED $33 BILLION ANNUALLY IN YIELD LOSS. WE HAVE RESEARCH THAT IS FOCUSED ON UNEARTHING THE MOLECULAR SECRETS OF PLANT-BACTERIAL INTERACTIONS THAT RESULT IN TWO IMPORTANT DISEASES OF VEGETABLES - BACTERIAL SOFT ROT OF ALL VEGETABLES AND BACTERIAL WILT OF CUCURBITS CROPS. RESEARCH HAS IDENTIFIED ACCESSIONS RESISTANT TO WILT DISEASE AND WHICH CAN BE EMPLOYED IN A BREEDING PROGRAM FOR RESISTANCE CULTIVARS. OTHER DISEASE RESEARCH IS EXAMINING THE USE OF BIOCONTROL AGENTS FOR DISEASE MANAGEMENT. THESE ALTERNATIVES TO CHEMICAL FUNGICIDES WILL PROVIDE TOOLS FOR DISEASE MANAGEMENT IN VEGETABLE PRODUCTION ESPECIALLY IN ORGANIC FARMING AND REDUCE USAGE OF TOXIC CHEMICALS IN CONVENTIONAL FARMING. INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) OF INSECT PESTS IS A HOLISTIC APPROACH TO SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE THAT FOCUSES ON MANAGING PESTS THROUGH A COMBINATION OF CULTURAL, PHYSICAL, BIOLOGICAL AND CHEMICAL METHODS. IPM IS A CROP PROTECTION PRACTICE THAT IS COST EFFECTIVE, ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND AND SOCIALLY ACCEPTABLE. TO FULFILL THIS NEED, WE CONDUCT RESEARCH FOCUSED ON CONDUCTING APPLIED RESEARCH EXPERIMENTS AND EDUCATING STAKEHOLDERS ON IPM THROUGH TRAINING AND PUBLICATIONS. IN-SERVICE TRAINING PROGRAMS FOR EXTENSION AGENTS AND IPM WORKSHOPS FOR OTHER STAKEHOLDERS ARE CONDUCTED ON STATE-WIDE BASIS IN EAST, MIDDLE AND WEST TENNESSEE REGIONS. IN OTHER INSECT RESEARCH, JAPANESE MAPLE SCALE RESEARCH, TIMED APPLICATIONS OF GROWTH REGULATORS AND ANNUAL MANAGEMENT PLANS DEVELOPED AT THE TSU NURSERY RESEARCH CENTER HAVE BEEN ADOPTED BY TENNESSEE GROWERS, REDUCING THE NUMBER OF REJECTED SHIPMENTS AND CULLED TREES. INVASIVE INSECTS ARE A MAJOR CONCERN IN NURSERY PRODUCTION. OUR RESEARCH IS PRODUCING DATA FOR NEW PESTICIDE REGULATIONS FOR FIRE ANT, JAPANESE BEETLE AND OTHER IMPORTANT INSECTS THAT ARE REDUCING WORKER EXPOSURE RISK, SAVING PRODUCERS TIME, AND OVERALL REDUCING THE COST OF PRODUCTION. MORE PRODUCER SAVINGS ARE EXPECTED WITH NEW PROTOCOLS UNDER DEVELOPMENT. SUSTAINABILITY RESEARCH WILL LEAD TO NEW PRACTICES THAT RESULTS IN REDUCTION OF INPUTS (PESTICIDES, FERTILIZER, WATER, LABOR, ETC.) IN THE NURSERY PRODUCTION SYSTEM, THUS ENHANCING THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE INDUSTRY, IMPROVING OUR ENVIRONMENT, REDUCING PRODUCTION COSTS FOR GROWERS, IMPROVING CROP QUALITY, AND BROADENING THE MARKET FOR TENNESSEE GREEN INDUSTRY PRODUCTS. TO ADDRESS THE WELL-BEING AND HEALTH OF INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES, RESEARCH IN FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES IS FOCUSED ON IMPROVING THE LIVES OF OUR STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH FCS EDUCATION, LEADERSHIP AND COMMUNICATION TO IMPROVE NOT ONLY THEIR HEALTH AND W ELL-BEING, BUT ALSO THEIR RELATIONSHIPS AND RESOURCES. THIS GROUP IS CONTINUING TO FOCUS ON EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS, LIVING WITH CHRONIC DISEASES, FOOD SECURITY VIA FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND OF COURSE, MITIGATING THE EFFECTS OF COVID-19 AS WE LIVE THROUGH THE P ANDEMIC. TSU AGRICULTURE IS PROUD OF THE RESEARCH CONDUCTED BY OUR FACULTY AND STAFF AS WE CONTINUE TO ADDRESS ISSUES THAT ARE CRITICAL TO THE WELFARE OF OUR STAKEHOLDERS, AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE PROSPERITY OF THE CITIZENS OF TENNESSEE, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. WE LOOK FORWARD TO CONTINUING TO FULFILL OUR UNIQUE ROLE AS AN HBCU LAND-GRANT INSTITUTION IN TENNESSEE AND TO CONTINUED GROWTH AND SUCCESS.
SBIR PHASE II PROPOSAL F2D-10467, UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEM (UAS) PAYLOADS FOR DETECTION OF SURFACE/BURIED ORDNANCE AND AERIAL INITIATION OF ENERGETICS

TRADITIONAL CROP BREEDING RELIES ON TIME-CONSUMING AND INEFFICIENT MANUAL FIELD OBSERVATIONS OR SAMPLINGS. UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLE (UAV)-BASED HIGH-THROUGHPUT PHENOTYPING PROMISES TO ALLEVIATE THE PHENOTYPING BOTTLENECK AND PROVIDE THE CAPABILITY FOR REPEATED NON-DESTRUCTIVE MEASUREMENT OF THOUSANDS OF GENOTYPES GROWN IN FIELD EXPERIMENT PLOTS IN CROP SELECTION CYCLES. MAJOR CHALLENGES REMAIN TO ENABLE MORE SOPHISTICATED ANALYSES AND DEVELOPMENT OF INTEGRATED DECISION-MAKING SYSTEMS THAT CAN GREATLY ACCELERATE CROP IMPROVEMENT AND PHENOTYPING. WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A DIGITAL RICE SELECTION SYSTEM THAT INTEGRATES UAV IMAGING, MACHINE LEARNING, AND MULTI-TRAIT DECISION-MAKING. OBJECTIVES ARE: 1) QUANTIFY KEY PHENOLOGICAL, MORPHOLOGICAL AND ARCHITECTURAL TRAITS THAT CAPTURE RICE GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT; 2) ACQUIRE MULTI-VIEWPOINT UAV IMAGES OF RICE GENOTYPES DURING CRITICAL GROWTH STAGES; 3) DEVELOP ADVANCED IMAGE ANALYSIS ALGORITHMS TO DERIVE KEY PHENOLOGICAL, MORPHOLOGICAL AND ARCHITECTURAL TRAITS FOR CRITICAL RICE GROWTH STAGES, AND 4) DEVELOP A DIGITAL RICE SELECTION SYSTEM THAT SCREENS FOR BEST-PERFORMING GENOTYPES THROUGH DATA INTEGRATION AND MULTI-TRAIT DECISION MAKING.GROUND TRUTH DATA FOR KEY TRAITS DURING CRITICAL RICE GROWTH STAGES WILL BE COLLECTED ALONG WITH HIGH-RESOLUTION RGB/MULTISPECTRAL UAV IMAGES FROM MULTIPLE CAMERA ANGLES. WE WILL DEVELOP (1) ADVANCED MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS TO EXTRACT KEY TRAITS, (2) MULTI-TRAIT-BASED MACHINE LEARNING MODELS TO ESTIMATE FINAL ABOVEGROUND BIOMASS AND GRAIN YIELD, AND (3) A MULTI-CRITERIA DECISION-MAKING SYSTEM TO SELECT BEST-PERFORMING RICE GENOTYPES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT REPRESENTS A MAJOR EFFORT IN DELIVERING AN INTEGRATED UAV IMAGERY-BASED DECISION-MAKING SYSTEM TO RICE BREEDERS AND RESEARCHERS AND WILL BE AN INDISPENSABLE TOOL TO GREATLY IMPROVE RICE BREEDING AND PHENOTYPING EFFICIENCY.

THE PROPOSED INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROJECT IS A MULTI-DISCIPLINARY (AGRONOMY, SOIL SCIENCE, PLANT PHYSIOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND ECONOMICS), MULTI-INSTITUTIONAL (TAMU AND NMSU) AND MULTI-LOCATION (TX AND NM) STUDY TO EVALUATE POTENTIAL FOR INCREASING CANOLA ACREAGE USING MARGINAL WATERS IN THE SOUTHERN GREAT PLAINS. OBJECTIVES OF THE STUDY ARE TO EVALUATE (I) CANOLA PERFORMANCE UNDER MARGINAL WATER IRRIGATION, (II) CHANGES TO ROOT ZONE SOIL PROPERTIES INCLUDING SALINITY, (III) IRRIGATION USE EFFICIENCY AND (IV) CANOLA CROP ECONOMIC FEASIBILITY. SEVERAL CULTIVARS OF CANOLA WILL BE EVALUATED FOR SALINITY TOLERANCE BY MEASURING GERMINATION, SEEDLING MORTALITY, EMERGENCE PERCENTAGE (EP) AND EMERGENCE INDEX, BIOMASS, AND SALT ACCUMULATION. SELECT SALT TOLERANT CULTIVARS PERFORMANCE WILL BE EVALUATED IN THE FIELD PLOTS AT TWO LOCATIONS, EL PASO, TX AND ARTESIA, NM. PLANT PERFORMANCE PARAMETERS SUCH AS NUMBER OF BRANCHES, SHOOT HEIGHT, PODS PER PLANT AND NUMBER OF SEEDS PER POD WILL BE MONITORED. PHYSIOLOGICAL PARAMETERS SUCH AS GAS EXCHANGE AND CHLOROPHYLL FLUORESCENCE, RELATIVE CHLOROPHYLL CONTENT WILL BE MEASURED. AT MATURITY PLANTS WILL BE HARVESTED AND BIOMASS, OIL SEED YIELD, OIL AND ASH CONTENT WILL BE DETERMINED. UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES (UAVS) EQUIPPED WITH HYPERSPECTRAL, MULTISPECTRAL BANDS, AND THERMAL SENSORS WILL BE USED TO DEVELOP EARLY DETECTION OF PLANT STRESSES TO TAKE CORRECTIVE ACTIONS TO REDUCE YIELD LOSSES. CHANGES TO ROOT ZONE SOIL PROPERTIES INCLUDING SALINITY WILL BE USED DEVELOP APPROPRIATE WATER AND SOIL SALINITY MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. ECONOMIC FEASIBILITY OF CANOLA PRODUCTION WILL BE EVALUATED BY CAREFULLY ASSESSING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATING COSTS, AS WELL AS POTENTIAL REVENUES.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** POOR CROP AND GRAZING MANAGEMENT PRACTICES HAVE DECREASED SOIL HEALTH AND CONTRIBUTED TO DECREASED PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY IN MUCH OF THE SOUTHERN GREAT PLAINS (SGP). ADOPTION OF ECOLOGICALLY SENSITIVE, LOW-COST CONSERVATION MANAGEMENT PRACTICES SUCH AS PASTURE CROPPING CAN POTENTIALLY ENHANCE HEALTH AND RESILIENCY OF DEGRADED SOILS. PASTURE CROPPING IS A FARMER-INITIATED, INNOVATIVE LAND MANAGEMENT SYSTEM THAT SEAMLESSLY INTEGRATES DIRECT SEEDING OF ANNUAL CROPS INTO DORMANT PERENNIAL GRASSES. ALTHOUGH THE SGP REGION PROVIDES AN EXCELLENT PLATFORM FOR THIS REGENERATIVE APPROACH THAT ORIGINATED IN AUSTRALIA, STUDIES EVALUATING SOIL HEALTH BENEFITS OF PASTURE CROPPING ARE LACKING.THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS STAKEHOLDER-DRIVEN STUDY IS TO EVALUATE IMPROVEMENTS IN SOIL-DEPENDENT ECOSYSTEM SERVICES WHEN GRASSLANDS ARE PASTURE CROPPED ON THE SGP. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO: 1) EVALUATE THE SOIL HEALTH BENEFITS OF PASTURE CROPPED PERENNIAL GRASSLANDS USING GROUND- AND UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLE (UAV) BASED MEASUREMENTS, 2) ASSESS THE RANCH- AND WATERSHED-SCALE IMPROVEMENTS IN ECOSYSTEM SERVICES FROM ADOPTION OF PASTURE CROPPING ON GRASSLANDS, AND 3) ANALYZE SHORT- AND LONG-TERM PROFITABILITY OF PASTURE CROPPING IN COMPARISON TO CONVENTIONAL PRACTICES UNDER DIFFERENT WEATHER AND MARKET CONDITIONS.WE WILL COMBINE FIELD EXPERIMENTS, UAV-BASED MEASUREMENTS, ENVIRONMENTAL MODELING AND ECONOMIC ANALYSES TO ACHIEVE THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS STUDY. PASTURE CROPPING FIELD EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CONDUCTED AT THE WEST TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY'S NANCE RANCH NEAR CANYON, TX IN RANDALL COUNTY AND AT THE DIXON WATER FOUNDATION'S PITTMAN RANCH NEAR MUENSTER, TX IN COOKE COUNTY. MODELING EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON THE HEADWATERS OF THE PRAIRIE DOG TOWN FORK OF THE RED RIVER WATERSHED IN THE TEXAS PANHANDLE, WHICH CONTAINS THE NANCE RANCH; AND THE CLEAR CREEK WATERSHED IN NORTH CENTRAL TEXAS, WHICH CONTAINS THE PITTMAN RANCH. THE FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY WILL BE INCORPORATED INTO AN IN-DEPTH GRAZING AND RANCH MANAGEMENT SCHOOL, AND PRESENTED AT VARIOUS SCIETIFIC AND STAKEHOLDER MEETINGS. WE EXPECT THAT THE QUANTIFICATION OF IMPROVEMENTS TO ECOSYSTEMS SERVICES AND PROFITABILITY DUE TO ADOPTION OF PASTURE CROPPING, AND ENHANCING PRODUCER/RANCHER AWARENESS WILL PROMOTE THE ADOPTION OF PASTURE CROPPING.

solicitations.title: COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH: VINES: TRACK 1: COEXISTENCE OF WIRELESS APPLICATIONS FOR DRONE HIGHWAYS -THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES OPERATION OF AUTONOMOUS UNCREWED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS COMMONLY REFERRED TO AS ?DRONES?, THAT COLLABORATE OVER WIRELESS COMMUNICATION NETWORKS ALONG ?DRONE HIGHWAYS? IN THE AIR. NON-COMMERCIAL APPLICATIONS INCLUDE EMERGENCY RESPONSE, PUBLIC SAFETY AND URBAN PLANNING, WHILE COMMERCIAL SERVICES SPAN E-COMMERCE, AGRICULTURE, AND TRAVEL. THE RADIO-FREQUENCY ENVIRONMENTS THAT DRONES NEED TO OPERATE IN ARE BECOMING INCREASINGLY COMPLEX AND CROWDED BECAUSE OF NUMEROUS APPLICATIONS THAT SHARE THE ELECTROMAGNETIC SPECTRUM. SIZE, WEIGHT, AND POWER ARE FUNDAMENTAL LIMITATIONS TO DRONE FUNCTIONALITY. THIS COLLABORATIVE PROJECT BETWEEN ELECTRICAL, COMPUTER AND AEROSPACE ENGINEERS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO BOULDER AND TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY WILL DEVELOP INTEGRATED COMMUNICATIONS AND SENSING SYSTEMS WITH HARDWARE INNOVATIONS THAT ENHANCE ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND ARE ESSENTIAL FOR SCALABLE, COST-EFFECTIVE DEPLOYMENT. AT THE HIGHER SYSTEM LEVEL, THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON AI-NATIVE SPECTRUM FORECASTING TO ENABLE LOCAL DECISION MAKING FOR COMMUNICATION ROBUSTNESS AND OPERATIONAL SAFETY. ENERGY EFFICIENCY IS ADDRESSED USING ANALOG PROCESSING, WHILE THE SIZE CONSTRAINT IS SOLVED BY DEVELOPMENT OF FUNCTIONALLY FLEXIBLE SMALL PHASED ARRAYS WITH NEW TYPES OF ISOLATION IN A HIGH-FREQUENCY ANALOG FRONT END AND POWER MANAGEMENT HARDWARE INTEGRATED INTO THE 5G/NEXTG GROUND NETWORK WITH SPECTRUM SHARING. THE RESEARCH CULMINATES IN HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE INTEGRATION WITH DRONE FLIGHT TESTING. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL LEAD TO A LEAP AHEAD IN TECHNOLOGY TO ENABLE SAFE AND EFFICIENT INTEGRATION OF DRONES INTO U.S. NATIONAL AIRSPACE LEVERAGING AN INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM OF ELECTRICAL AND COMPUTER ENGINEERS, COMPUTER SCIENTISTS AND AEROSPACE ENGINEERS ACROSS TWO UNIVERSITIES. THE PROPOSED NOVEL HARDWARE IN THE LOWER FR3 RANGE IS SCALABLE TO OTHER FREQUENCY BANDS AND HAS THE POTENTIAL TO ESTABLISH THE NEW BACKGROUND FOR NETWORK INFRASTRUCTURE THAT WILL GUARANTEED SAFE TRANSPORTATION, QUICK EMERGENCY RESPONSE WITH RATIONALIZED CONSUMPTION OF ENERGY RESOURCES. THE INVESTIGATORS ARE MEMBERS OF NATIONAL SCIENCE FOUNDATION CENTERS, WHICH FACILITATES INDUSTRY COLLABORATIONS AND RESEARCH RESULT DISSEMINATION. THE RESEARCH IS INTEGRATED IN SEVERAL COURSES THAT HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO IMPROVE STEM STUDENT RETENTION. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE NOT PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.

CAREER: FACILITATING AUTONOMY OF ROBOTS THROUGH LEARNING-BASED CONTROL -DRONE TECHNIQUES HAVE ACHIEVED SIGNIFICANT PROGRESS IN THE PAST DECADES. HOWEVER, IT IS STILL VERY CHALLENGING TO MASSIVELY BRING HETEROGENEOUS DRONES BY MANY DIFFERENT MANUFACTURERS TO REAL-WORLD APPLICATIONS. ONE MAIN REASON IS THAT, WHENEVER A NEW DRONE IS BUILT, THE PLANNING AND CONTROL ALGORITHMS FOR THE DRONE USUALLY HAVE TO BE DESIGNED VERY CAREFULLY AND THE ACTIONS FOR THE DRONE TO TAKE USUALLY HAVE TO BE LABORIOUSLY PROGRAMMED WITH CONSIDERABLE TUNING EFFORT. TO REMOVE, IF NOT LESSEN, SUCH LIMITATIONS, THIS FACULTY EARLY CAREER DEVELOPMENT (CAREER) PROJECT ESTABLISHES A NOVEL LEARNING-BASED FRAMEWORK THAT EQUIPS DRONES WITH NEW CAPABILITIES OF LEARNING FROM THE EXPERIENCE OF OTHER DRONES DESPITE THEIR DIFFERENT DYNAMICS AND PLATFORMS. THIS APPROACH TO DESIGN OF PLANNING AND CONTROL OF DRONES WILL SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE THE DESIGN, TEST, EVALUATION AND CERTIFICATION OF DRONES, UNIQUELY AND EFFICIENTLY CUSTOMIZED FOR APPLICATIONS IN THEIR OPERATING ENVIRONMENT. THE INTEGRATED RESEARCH-AND-EDUCATION ACTIVITIES WILL PROVIDE STUDENTS IN THE WESTERN NEW YORK AREA WITH HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE AND INTERNSHIP OPPORTUNITIES ON DRONE TECHNIQUES, TOWARD BETTER PREPARING THE FUTURE WORKFORCE FOR THE UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEM INDUSTRY IN THE UNITED STATES. THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A NOVEL LEARNING-BASED FEEDFORWARD CONTROL FRAMEWORK AND EQUIP DRONES WITH NEW CAPABILITIES FOR LEARNING THREE PARTICULAR SKILLS, I.E., (1) HOW TO GENERATE A DYNAMICALLY FEASIBLE TRAJECTORY, (2) HOW TO SENSE AND COMPENSATE EXTERNAL DISTURBANCES, AND (3) HOW TO LEARN FROM OTHERS' LEARNED EXPERIENCE, CALLED DYNAMIC LEARNING. THESE THREE SKILLS ARE CRUCIAL FOR DRONES TO PERFORM COMPLEX TASKS, AND THE FOUNDATION FOR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW ONE ROBOT COULD EFFICIENTLY LEARN FROM THE EXPERIENCES GATHERED BY OTHER ROBOTS WITH DIFFERENT DYNAMICS. KEY TO THIS APPROACH IS AN ARCHITECTURE THAT AUTOMATICALLY ADJUSTS THE ORIGINAL OUTPUTS OF THE BASELINE PLANNERS AND CONTROLLERS BY ADDING FEEDFORWARD LEARNING SIGNALS TO IMPROVE DRONE'S FLIGHT PERFORMANCE. THIS LEARNING FRAMEWORK IS NEITHER TO COMPLETELY REPLACE THE EXISTING PLANNING AND CONTROL METHODS NOR TO COMPETE FOR THE HIGHEST OPTIMIZED PERFORMANCE POSSIBLE BUT RATHER TO PROVIDE AN ELEGANT LEARNING MECHANISM THAT IS HIGHLY ADAPTABLE AND REASONABLY EFFICIENT INVOLVING MINIMAL HARDWARE MODIFICATION AND SOFTWARE RECONFIGURATION FOR COMMODITY DRONES. THIS PROJECT IS SUPPORTED BY THE CROSS-DIRECTORATE FOUNDATIONAL RESEARCH IN ROBOTICS PROGRAM, JOINTLY MANAGED AND FUNDED BY THE DIRECTORATES FOR ENGINEERING (ENG) AND COMPUTER AND INFORMATION SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING (CISE). THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE NOT PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.

solicitations.title: CAREER: SIM-INTEGRATED AIR-TO-GROUND AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE NETWORKS -EXISTING VEHICULAR NETWORKS FREQUENTLY FALL SHORT OF THE ABILITY TO PROCESS AND TRANSMIT LARGE VOLUMES OF DATA WITH ULTRA-LOW LATENCY, HIGH RELIABILITY, AND LOW ENERGY CONSUMPTION. THIS PROJECT DEVELOPS AND EVALUATES A NOVEL AIR-TO-GROUND VEHICULAR NETWORK TO OVERCOME ENERGY AND LATENCY BOTTLENECKS AT THE MOBILE EDGE, LEVERAGING UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES (UAVS) AS MOBILE COMMUNICATION AND COMPUTING PLATFORMS TO PROVIDE ON-DEMAND SERVICES. ADDITIONALLY, SELECTED SIGNAL-PROCESSING TASKS ARE MOVED FROM POWER-HUNGRY DIGITAL HARDWARE TO ANALOG DOMAIN BY EXPLORING PROGRAMMABLE STACKED INTELLIGENT METASURFACE (SIM) ANTENNAS TO FURTHER IMPROVE ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND RESILIENCE. THE SYSTEM IS OPTIMIZED BY AI-DRIVEN RESOURCE ALLOCATION, UAV TRAJECTORY PLANNING, AND VEHICLE OFFLOADING STRATEGIES. IT ENHANCES INTELLIGENT TRANSPORTATION SYSTEMS, SUPPORTS SAFER TRANSPORTATION, AND IMPROVES COMMUNICATION DURING EMERGENCIES. THE PROJECT CONTAINS AN INTEGRATED EDUCATION PLAN INCLUDING UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH ENGAGEMENT, NEW GRADUATE COURSES, DRONE CODING AND TRAFFIC SAFETY CHALLENGES. IT ALSO DEVELOPS A DISASTER-RELIEF POP-UP CONNECTIVITY KIT FOR EMERGENCY COMMUNICATION SCENARIOS, AND RELEASES DATASETS AND OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE FRAMEWORK FOR SIM-INTEGRATED AIR-TO-GROUND AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE NETWORKS AND INVESTIGATES HOW PROGRAMMABLE WAVE-DOMAIN BEAMFORMING, UAV-ASSISTED VEHICULAR EDGE COMPUTING, AND AI-DRIVEN RESOURCE ALLOCATION CAN BE JOINTLY DESIGNED FOR UPLINK TASK OFFLOADING AND DOWNLINK SERVICE DELIVERY IN HIGHLY MOBILE WIRELESS ENVIRONMENTS. THE RESEARCH AGENDA IS ORGANIZED INTO THREE THRUSTS: (1) DEVELOPING A PREDICTIVE, MULTI-AGENT SPATIOTEMPORAL INTELLIGENCE SCHEME TO PREDICT MOBILITY AND SIM-AWARE QUALITY OF SERVICE; (2) DESIGNING SCALABLE AI-DRIVEN CONTROL METHODS TO JOINTLY OPTIMIZE UAV POSITIONING, VEHICLE TASK OFFLOADING, RADIO RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND SIM CONFIGURATIONS FOR ENERGY-EFFICIENT UPLINK TRANSMISSIONS; AND (3) DEVELOPING HIERARCHICAL SCHEMES USING ADVANCED REINFORCEMENT LEARNING TO ADAPT WIRELESS RESOURCES FOR DOWNLINK OPTIMIZATION UNDER DYNAMIC TRAFFIC AND WIRELESS CONDITIONS. VALIDATION IS PERFORMED WITH SIMULATION, HARDWARE-IN-THE-LOOP TESTING, AND STAGED EXPERIMENTS. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE NOT PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.

REU SITE: APPLIED COMPUTING RESEARCH IN UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEMS -TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY-CORPUS CHRISTI, LOCATED ON THE TEXAS GULF COAST AND A FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION (FAA)-APPROVED SITE FOR UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEMS (UAS), WILL CONTINUE TO OFFER A TEN-WEEK SUMMER RESEARCH EXPERIENCE IN UAS TECHNOLOGY TO TEN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS EACH YEAR. STUDENTS ARE SELECTED THROUGH A NATIONWIDE RECRUITMENT PROCESS AIMED AT ATTRACTING HIGHLY TALENTED UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN COMPUTING OR RELATED DISCIPLINES. THIS UNIQUE RESEARCH EXPERIENCE EXPOSES UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCHERS TO A WIDE RANGE OF UAS APPLICATIONS, ADDRESSING REGIONAL AND NATIONAL CHALLENGES SUCH AS COASTAL MANAGEMENT, COASTAL ECOLOGY, HUMAN SAFETY, PRECISION AGRICULTURE, AND UAS TECHNOLOGY SECURITY. THE PROGRAM INCLUDES MENTORING BY EXPERIENCED FACULTY, SKILL-BUILDING SEMINARS AND WORKSHOPS, RESEARCH PRESENTATIONS, GRADUATE SCHOOL PREPARATION, AND OTHER PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES. THE OBJECTIVE OF THE PROGRAM IS TO PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH VALUABLE RESEARCH EXPERIENCES IN A DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT FOCUSED ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF SECURE, AUTONOMOUS UAS TECHNOLOGY. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE RESEARCH IN APPLIED COMPUTING FOR UAS-BASED APPLICATIONS, ALONG WITH SKILL-BUILDING SESSIONS DESIGNED TO ENHANCE GROUP COHESIVENESS AND REFINE TECHNICAL WRITING, COMMUNICATION, AND RESEARCH SKILLS. PARTICIPANTS WILL WRITE AND SUBMIT RESEARCH PAPERS ON THEIR WORK FOR PRESENTATION AT LOCAL, REGIONAL, AND NATIONAL SYMPOSIUMS. WATER SCARCITY THREATENS AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY IN SEMI-ARID REGIONS WITH DEPLETING IRRIGATION RESOURCES. COTTON AND SORGHUM ARE DROUGHT TOLERANT AND CAN ENHANCE PROFITABILITY AND SOIL HEALTH IN WATER-CONSTRAINED SYSTEMS. HOWEVER, INTEGRATING THESE CROPS INTO A UNIFIED CROPPING SYSTEM, ESPECIALLY REGARDING OPTIMAL IRRIGATION PRACTICES WHEN BOTH CROPS ARE GROWN TOGETHER, DEMANDS FURTHER INVESTIGATION.THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO ENHANCE AGRICULTURAL RESILIENCE AND WATER USE EFFICIENCY IN THE TEXAS HIGH PLAINS BY OPTIMIZING A COTTON-SORGHUM CROPPING SYSTEM. THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO: 1) DETERMINE OPTIMAL PLANTING DATES AND CROP VARIETIES FOR MAXIMIZING YIELD AND WATER USE EFFICIENCY; 2) EVALUATE IRRIGATION STRATEGIES AND ECONOMIC RETURNS AT VARIOUS SCALES AND SOIL TYPES; 3) USE REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGY TO MONITOR CROP GROWTH AND IMPROVE IRRIGATION MANAGEMENT; AND 4) IMPLEMENT EXTENSION PROGRAMS TO DISSEMINATE FINDINGS AND PROMOTE ADOPTION AMONG FARMERS.THE STUDY WILL INVOLVE SMALL PLOT EXPERIMENTS IN THE TEXAS HIGH PLAINS, USING ADVANCED TECHNOLOGIES, INCLUDING SATELLITE AND UAV IMAGERY, FOR REAL-TIME MONITORING. THE DATA WILL BE INCORPORATED INTO THE DSSAT MODELING SYSTEM TO PREDICT OPTIMAL IRRIGATION STRATEGIES AND ECONOMIC OUTCOMES. COLLABORATIVE EFFORTS WITH LOCAL PRODUCERS WILL TEST THESE STRATEGIES IN COMMERCIAL SETTINGS. THIS RESEARCH SEEKS TO PROVIDE ACTIONABLE INSIGHTS FOR IMPROVING WATER MANAGEMENT AND CROP PROFITABILITY, CONTRIBUTING TO THE LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY OF AGRICULTURE IN WATER-SCARCE REGIONS.THIS PROPOSAL ADDRESSES AFRI 2024 - A1811 (TOPIC 18): DEVELOPING IRRIGATION SCHEDULING TECHNOLOGIES TO MAXIMIZE WATER-USE EFFICIENCY WHILE OPTIMIZING PROFITABILITY OF CROPPING SYSTEMS FOR COTTON AND SORGHUM IN THE SAME FIELD.

COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH: MARITIME TO INLAND TRANSITIONS TOWARDS ENVIRONMENTS FOR CONVECTION INITIATION (MITTEN CI) -THE GOAL OF THE MARITIME TO INLAND TRANSITIONS TOWARDS ENVIRONMENTS FOR CONVECTION INITIATION (MITTEN-CI) CAMPAIGN IS TO DEVELOP THE MOST THOROUGH UNDERSTANDING TO DATE OF TRANSITIONS IN NEAR-SURFACE THERMODYNAMIC AND WIND PROFILE STRUCTURE DUE TO INLAND MOVEMENT OF MARINE AIR IN THE GREAT LAKES COASTAL ENVIRONMENT, AND RESULTANT IMPACTS ON THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT. UNDERSTANDING SUCH TRANSITIONS AND THEIR IMPLICATIONS FOR THUNDERSTORMS HAS SUBSTANTIAL BROADER IMPACTS, GIVEN THE SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF THE HUMAN POPULATION THAT LIVES IN COASTAL AREAS. HYPOTHESES ARE DEVELOPED TO TARGET NOVEL ASPECTS OF NEAR-SHORE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT AND EVOLUTION OF NEAR-SURFACE PROFILES OF TEMPERATURE, HUMIDITY, AND WIND THAT HAVE RECEIVED RELATIVELY LITTLE ATTENTION AND ENABLE OPERATIONS UNDER A WIDE RANGE OF BACKGROUND WEATHER PATTERNS, RESULTING IN A HIGH PROBABILITY OF SUCCESS IN THE CAMPAIGN?S GOALS. THE MITTEN-CI CAMPAIGN WILL RESULT IN AN EXTENSIVE DATASET THAT CHARACTERIZES THE TEMPORAL EVOLUTION OF OVER-LAKE THERMODYNAMIC AND KINEMATIC PROFILES USING UNCREWED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS (UAS), IN ADDITION TO THOROUGH SAMPLING OF BOUNDARY LAYER SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL VARIABILITY OVER LAND USING INSTRUMENTATION ALONG A 120 KM SHORE-PERPENDICULAR TRANSECT WITH SIX FLUX TOWERS, TWO MOBILE MESONETS, MULTIPLE RADIOSONDE LAUNCH SITES, A DOPPLER LIDAR, AND TWO MOBILE KA-BAND DOPPLER RADARS. THESE DATA WILL ENABLE HYPOTHESIS TESTING THAT WILL RESULT IN NEW KNOWLEDGE OF PROCESSES ACROSS A RANGE OF SCALES THAT RESULT IN CONVECTION INITIATION (CI) OR FAILURE THEREOF IN MIDLATITUDE COASTAL REGIONS. SPECIFIC ASPECTS OF COASTAL CONVECTIVE ENVIRONMENTS AND CI TO BE INVESTIGATED INCLUDE DEVELOPMENT OF LAKE-BREEZE MAHTES (MESOSCALE AIRMASSES WITH HIGH THETA-E), I.E., INSTABILITY MAXIMA ON THE COOL SIDE OF LAKE-BREEZE FRONTS (LBFS), THE POTENTIAL FOR DIFFUSE LBFS TO EXIST EMBEDDED WITHIN SYNOPTIC-SCALE ONSHORE FLOW AND INFLUENCE CI, LBF MISOVORTEX INFLUENCE ON CI BOTH INDEPENDENTLY AND THROUGH INTERACTIONS WITH HORIZONTAL CONVECTIVE ROLLS, RKW THEORY?S RELATION TO LBF CI, AND THE INFLUENCE OF ENTRAINMENT ON LBF THERMODYNAMICS, STRUCTURE, AND PROPAGATION. SIGNIFICANT NEW KNOWLEDGE OF PROCESSES RELATED TO MAHTE DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED AND WILL INFORM BROADER RESEARCH ON MAHTE DEVELOPMENT IN OTHER TYPES OF FRONTAL BOUNDARIES WHICH ARE MORE DIFFICULT TO STUDY WITHOUT A NOMADIC CAMPAIGN. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE NOT PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** OUR PROJECT IS DEDICATED TO ADVANCING PRECISION AGRICULTURE IN THE SOUTHERN GREAT PLAINS REGION, ADDRESSING THE CRUCIAL ISSUE OF SUSTAINABLE FARMING. PRECISION AGRICULTURE, WHICH INCORPORATES CUTTING-EDGE TECHNOLOGIES LIKE UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEMS (UAS) AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, ALLOWS FOR THE COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS OF HIGH-RESOLUTION DATA ON SOIL PROPERTIES, CROP CHARACTERISTICS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS. BY IMPLEMENTING PRECISION AGRICULTURE PRACTICES, FARMERS CAN MAKE DATA-DRIVEN DECISIONS TO OPTIMIZE RESOURCE ALLOCATION, INCREASE CROP YIELDS, AND MINIMIZE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT.THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THIS RESEARCH EXTENDS BEYOND THE AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITY, AS IT DIRECTLY IMPACTS ECONOMIC STABILITY, ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION, AND FOOD SECURITY IN THE BROADER COMMUNITY. AS WE WORK TOWARDS THESE GOALS, OUR PROJECT GOES BEYOND SIMPLE RESEARCH. WE ARE COMMITTED TO SHARING KNOWLEDGE THROUGH EDUCATION AND TRAINING, PLAYING A KEY ROLE IN PROMOTING THE ADOPTION OF PRECISION AGRICULTURE PRACTICES.IN LINE WITH OUR MISSION, WE WILL DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE NEW COURSE THAT FOCUSES ON UAS APPLICATIONS IN PRECISION AGRICULTURE. THIS COURSE WILL EQUIP THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS WITH THE NECESSARY KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS TO DRIVE INNOVATION AND SUSTAINABILITY IN THE FIELD. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL PROVIDE COHORT TRAINING ACTIVITIES, OFFERING HANDS-ON EXPERIENCES AND PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS TO ENHANCE UNDERSTANDING AND PROFICIENCY IN PRECISION AGRICULTURE TECHNIQUES.THROUGH THESE EDUCATIONAL AND TRAINING EFFORTS, WE AIM TO EMPOWER FARMERS WITH ACTIONABLE INSIGHTS, FOSTERING PRODUCTIVITY WHILE MINIMIZING RESOURCE WASTE. EMPHASIZING THE ADOPTION OF PRECISION AGRICULTURE TECHNIQUES WILL LEAD TO IMPROVED WATER USE EFFICIENCY, BETTER PRESERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES, AND ULTIMATELY, A MORE RESILIENT AND SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR. WE HOPE TO CREATE A POSITIVE IMPACT NOT ONLY FOR FARMERS BUT FOR THE BROADER COMMUNITY AS WELL, CONTRIBUTING TO ECONOMIC GROWTH, ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, AND ENSURING A STEADY AND RELIABLE FOOD SUPPLY FOR GENERATIONS TO COME.

solicitations.title: COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH: FRAMEWORKS: BUILDING THE TWENTY-FIRST CENTURY CITIZEN SCIENCE FRAMEWORK TO ENABLE SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY ACROSS DISCIPLINES -TWENTY-FIRST CENTURY RESEARCH IS ENABLED BY THE AVAILABILITY OF VAST AMOUNTS OF DATA, COLLECTED ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF TEMPORAL AND SPATIAL SCALES, OFTEN IN REAL TIME. ENTIRE FLEETS OF SATELLITES, DRONES AND OTHER DEVICES MONITOR THE EARTH AT EVER-INCREASING RESOLUTION, ADDING TO THE ENORMOUS CORPUS OF MAPS AND METADATA THAT ENABLE SCIENCES FROM GEOLOGY TO BIODIVERSITY. WHILE CITIZEN SCIENCE - OR CROWDSOURCING SCIENCE - HAS BEEN SUCCESSFULLY LEVERAGED OVER THE PAST SEVERAL DECADES TO CLOSE THE ANALYSIS GAP ARISING FROM LARGE AMOUNTS OF DATA, THE SHEER SCALE AND COMPLEXITY OF THESE NEW DATA SETS PRESENTS NEW CHALLENGES. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THESE CHALLENGES THROUGH NOVEL CITIZEN SCIENCE CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE (CSCI) WHERE NEW TOOLS AND TECHNIQUES, INCLUDING TEAMING HUMANS WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), ARE BEING DEVELOPED TO ENABLE RESEARCHERS TO EFFICIENTLY EXTRACT THE BEST RESULTS FROM LARGE AND COMPLEX DATA SETS. THIS EFFORT INCORPORATES MAPPING, MACHINE LEARNING, AND DATA SHARING INNOVATIONS IN BIODIVERSITY, GEOSCIENCE, AND ASTRONOMY RESEARCH AND EXPANDS THE CAPACITY OF RESEARCH COMMUNITIES ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF DISCIPLINES TO USE CITIZEN SCIENCE AS A SUITABLE, OPEN AND SUSTAINABLE RESEARCH METHODOLOGY. THIS PROJECT LEVERAGES NSF-SUPPORTED CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE, INCLUDING THE ZOONIVERSE CITIZEN SCIENCE PLATFORM WITH ITS NEARLY THREE MILLION VOLUNTEERS, TO PROVIDE A NOVEL CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE BY: (1) INTEGRATING MAPPING INFRASTRUCTURE INTO ZOONIVERSE TO ACCELERATE ACCURATE PROCESSING AND CURATION OF OFTEN COMPLEX DATA SETS FOR GEOSCIENCE AND BIODIVERSITY PROJECTS; (2) PROVIDING AN INCUBATOR HUB FOR RESEARCHERS AND DEVELOPERS TO DESIGN AND DEPLOY INNOVATIVE CITIZEN SCIENCE PROJECTS WITH A FAST PRODUCTION TURN-AROUND PARTICULARLY FOR AI TRAINING; AND (3) PROVIDING CYBER-PATHWAYS TO EXISTING CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE, CREATING DOCUMENTATION FOR ZOONIVERSE PROJECTS TO RESPONSIBLY DEPOSIT THEIR DATA INTO APPROPRIATE REPOSITORIES, AND FACILITATING WORKSHOPS FOR ZOONIVERSE PROJECT TEAMS TO DEVELOP BEST PRACTICES FOR DATA AND MODEL SHARING. TO ENSURE WIDE DISSEMINATION OF THE NEW CSCI, A STRONG COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE IS ENGAGED AND SUPPORTED THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT EFFORT. THE PROJECT IS LED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA IN COLLABORATION WITH THE ADLER PLANETARIUM AND THE UNIVERSITY OF OXFORD, AS CORE ZOONIVERSE INSTITUTIONS AND ASTROPHYSICS EXPERTISE, AND JOINED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA AND THE FLORIDA MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY WITH EXPERTISE IN BIODIVERSITY, MUSEUM SPECIMEN COLLECTIONS, AND DATA REPOSITORIES, AS WELL AS NORTHERN ARIZONA UNIVERSITY WITH EXPERTISE IN EARTH SCIENCES, MAPPING CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE, AND THE STUDY OF THE ANTARCTICA?S DRY VALLEYS. AS THE LARGEST CITIZEN SCIENCE PLATFORM, AND WITH KEY TOOLS FOR HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP DATA ANALYSIS TASKS, THE ZOONIVERSE IS UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO DEVELOP SKILLS AND BEST PRACTICES TO LOWER THE BARRIER FOR RESEARCH TEAMS TO RESPONSIBLY SHARE DATA AND MODELS. THIS IS CARRIED OUT THROUGH FACT-FINDING AND DEMONSTRATION WITH SEVERAL KEY GROUPS WHO ARE EXEMPLARS IN THE DATA AND MODEL SHARING ECOSYSTEM, INCLUDING GITHUB, THE NATIONAL SCIENCE DATA FABRIC (NSDF), THE GLOBAL BIODIVERSITY INFORMATION FACILITY (GBIF), AND OPEN SCIENCE CHAIN. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.
